newsitem.title: USA: Chattanooga, Hamilton Cty, Tenn., merge schools.
newsitem.headline: Chattanooga, Hamilton Cty, Tenn., merge schools.

text.p: Tennessee's Hamilton County and City of Chattanooga merged their school systems this week despite a pending lawsuit aimed at stopping the merger.
The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court Monday, challenging the city's right to give school buildings to the county without putting the question before voters.
Voters did approve the consolidation in a 1994 referendum, but the plaintiffs said the ballot wording was confusing and did not clearly address building ownership.
City residents successfully petitioned for a re-vote last year. The subsequent referendum asked voters to decide whether a new vote was needed, and voters said no.

The consolidation plan calls for the Hamilton County School Board to oversee 45,000 students and 4,000 employees in 80 schools. It includes construction of six new schools using proceeds from a recent $53 million general obligation bond issue.
Chattanooga is the state's fourth largest city. The three bigger ones -- Nashville, Memphis and Knoxville -- also have consolidated school systems with their counties.
